storage: Keep in an airtight jar, away from other spices because the smell spreads; room temperature, dry and out of sunlight; use within about a year.
looksLike: A fine pale-yellow powder (or lumps of brownish resin) with a very strong sulphur-like smell that mellows into an onion-garlic flavour once fried in hot oil.
howToPick: Buy a sealed airtight bottle or jar; the smell should be strong and sharp even through the pack. A weak smell means a lot of filler or old stock. Wheat-containing blends are common, so check the label if you avoid gluten.
shelfLife: Several months to a year in a tight container; the aroma fades with air (general guidance, not taken from a source in this run).
substitutes: Garlic and onion (finely chopped, fried first)
mergeNotes: Range 1179.6–2915.7 was wider than 30% of avg 1924.6; narrowed to ±15%.
